name: Subscription Revenue Recovery
description: Find recurring-revenue leakage, connect it to rep attribution when the data supports it, quantify recovery scenarios, and publish a CEO-ready dashboard and page brief. Read-only: it proposes interventions but never changes customers, subscriptions, orders, reps, or campaigns.

steps.name: Map retention evidence
steps.prompt:
Build a fresh evidence map for this company's subscription-retention analysis. This is a read-only discovery step.

1. Call `db_schema` with `mode: "overview"`. Then call `db_schema` searches for `subscription`, `order`, `payment`, `rep`, `referr`, `sponsor`, and `affiliate`. Use `mode: "tables"` on the smallest set of candidate tables needed to understand subscription status, recurring amount and cadence, orders or payment attempts, customer identity, and rep/referral attribution. Do not guess names from another company or a prior run.
2. Use bounded SELECT-only `db_query` calls to establish record counts, minimum and maximum event dates, status values, null coverage for the important fields, and the newest source timestamp. Never use `SELECT *`; name columns and cap detail samples.
3. Write a join map with fully qualified table and column names for: subscription -> customer; subscription -> order/payment event; customer/order/subscription -> acquiring or credited rep/referrer. Mark a path `unavailable` when the schema cannot establish it. Similar names are not proof of a join.
4. Choose one analysis window from the evidence: prefer the latest complete 90 days; shorten it only when the dataset is younger and say why. Record the exact inclusive start and exclusive end timestamps. Separate observed facts from assumptions. Empty or missing subscription data is a valid finding, not a reason to invent a substitute.
5. Do not call a mutating tool or issue non-SELECT SQL. Do not expose customer email, phone, street address, payment data, or other customer PII in the output.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` followed by a compact object containing `window`, `freshness`, `tables`, `joins`, `coverage_counts`, `status_values`, `currency_basis`, `data_gaps`, and `assumptions`. If no usable subscription data exists, set `subscription_analysis_available: false` and explain the exact missing evidence.
acceptance: The report names the exact inclusive start and exclusive end timestamps, the newest source timestamp, subscription record count, and whether the source covers the full intended window.

Every table, column, and join used later is identified from live `db_schema` evidence with a fully qualified name; any unavailable subscription, payment, or rep-attribution path is explicitly marked unavailable rather than guessed.
Bounded SELECT-only queries establish status values, date coverage, important-field null coverage, and currency basis without returning customer contact, address, or payment PII.
The output distinguishes observed facts, calculated values, assumptions, and data gaps, including an honest no-subscription-data branch when necessary.

steps.name: Quantify lifecycle leakage
acceptance: Live SELECT-only queries independently reproduce the reported lifecycle-status counts and recurring-value totals for the exact evidence-map window.
Involuntary payment exposure is kept separate from paused, cancelled, expired, and unknown value; the report never calls all non-active value recoverable revenue.
Monthly normalization states its formula and uses only records with amount plus interval unit/count; different currencies remain separate unless a documented base-currency field is used.
Headline totals reconcile to the status-level evidence with the delta shown, and missing lifecycle, cycle, payment-event, or plan evidence is reported rather than inferred.

steps.name: Trace rep attribution
acceptance: The report uses a schema-proven attribution join or explicitly returns `attribution_available: false`; it never treats similar rep/referrer/sponsor field names as interchangeable without evidence.
Every rep cohort rate includes its numerator and denominator, low-volume cohorts are not over-ranked, and the output contains no subscriber contact, address, or payment PII.
Attributed plus unattributed subscription counts and recurring value reconcile to the eligible population for each currency, with any delta shown.
The report labels attribution meaning and causality limits honestly and performs no rep-credit, order, subscription, message, campaign, or incentive mutation.

steps.name: Model recovery value
steps.prompt:
Turn the verified lifecycle and attribution evidence into one prioritized, quantified recovery model. This remains analysis-only.

Read the completed outputs from `lifecycle-leakage` and `rep-attribution`, including any needs-review findings. Do not hide a needs-review or unavailable branch. Re-check only the smallest live aggregates needed to resolve contradictions; do not silently replace an upstream result.

Produce:
1. A baseline table by currency: active normalized recurring value, involuntary payment exposure, paused value, cancellations in-window, and the exact record counts behind each amount. Never sum currencies.
2. Three transparent sensitivity scenarios applied ONLY to the eligible involuntary-exposure base: 5%, 10%, and 20% recovery. Label all three `Scenario assumption — not forecast`. Show the formula (`eligible exposure x assumed recovery rate`) and both monthly and annualized values; annualized means `monthly x 12`, not observed annual revenue. If there is no amount field, use counts and omit dollar scenarios.
3. A ranked intervention plan with no more than three moves: payment-retry/dunning review, paused-member save review, early-cycle cancellation review, or rep-led outreach/coaching only when the evidence supports it. For each, name the eligible population, live value base, owner, success metric, holdout or before/after measurement, and the approval/write that would be required to execute it.
4. A CEO-ready headline that states one observed exposure number and one clearly labeled scenario value. Also provide a conservative alternative headline that uses counts when currency/value evidence is incomplete.

Hard rules: do not claim modeled value is recovered revenue; do not invent a recovery rate, causal explanation, or industry benchmark; do not expose PII; do not mutate Fluid data or contact anyone. Any execution is a separate follow-up that requires explicit user approval after reviewing this analysis.

End with `STEP_OUTPUT:` containing `baseline`, `scenarios`, `ranked_interventions`, `ceo_headlines`, `measurement_plan`, `write_actions_requiring_approval`, `data_gaps`, and `assumptions`.
acceptance: The baseline uses only live upstream evidence, keeps currencies separate, names record counts behind amounts, and does not treat paused or cancelled value as involuntary-payment exposure.
The 5%, 10%, and 20% cases are visibly labeled scenario assumptions rather than forecasts, use the shown eligible-exposure formula, and annualize only by multiplying a monthly value by 12.
Each of at most three interventions names an evidence-backed eligible population, success metric, measurement method, accountable owner, and the exact future write/action requiring explicit approval.
The CEO headline distinguishes observed exposure from modeled opportunity, supplies a count-based fallback, contains no PII, and claims no action or recovery that did not occur.

steps.name: Publish recovery dashboard
acceptance: `list_dashboards` shows a saved dashboard titled `Subscription Revenue Recovery`, and the deliverable reports its id when available plus the exact data-as-of timestamp and evidence window.

Dashboard headline, status, scenario, attribution, and intervention values reproduce the recovery-model output, keep currencies separate, use raw numeric metrics with format hints, use dollar formatters only for verified USD values, label every other numeric currency metric with its ISO code, and expose no subscriber PII.
Every modeled value is visibly labeled `Scenario assumption — not forecast`; unavailable attribution or currency evidence becomes a visible data-quality banner rather than an invented card.

The CEO value page brief is under 350 words, contains all seven required sections, directly separates live observations from modeled scenarios, and states the approval boundary and `fluid_writes_performed: false`.

steps.name: Review CEO readiness
acceptance: The saved `Subscription Revenue Recovery` dashboard exists and its observed headline count/value is independently reproducible from bounded SELECT-only live queries for the stated window and freshness.
Currencies remain separate, the eligible exposure base is reproduced, and 5%/10%/20% values are correct sensitivity arithmetic visibly labeled assumptions rather than forecasts or achieved revenue.
The handoff includes the verified rep-attribution result or exact gap, no hidden needs-review findings or PII, three approval-gated actions with success metrics, and a three-beat demo path.

The final CEO page copy stays under 350 words, distinguishes live proof from modeled upside, says no Fluid writes/interventions were performed, and explicitly requires user approval before any execution.
